newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra cites grocery, new products gains.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra cites grocery, new products gains.

text.p: ConAgra Inc said Tuesday its record fiscal 1997 fourth quarter and full year sales and earnings benefited from strong results at its grocery products division and new product introductions.
ConAgra reported that earnings for its fiscal year ended May 25, 1997 rose 14.5 percent from a year ago to $2.68 a share from $2.34 in fiscal 1996.
Sales increased to $24 billion from $23.90 billion in fiscal 1996. Business dispositions and restructuring actions cut fiscal 1997 sales by about $1.05 billion from fiscal 1996.
In ConAgra's grocery and diversified products industry segment, operating profit rose 15.6 percent to $810.3 million in fiscal 1997. Sales were up eight percent to $5.33 billion.
In fiscal 1997, ConAgra frozen foods introduced 28 new products, generated unit volume growth and significantly increased full-year operating profit.

Hunt-Wesson increased unit volumes modestly in fiscal 1997 and showed good earnings growth. Hunt-Wesson's and ConAgra frozen foods' earnings fell as expected in the fourth quarter, in part due to spending on new products designed to spur volume growth in fiscal 1998.
The Lamb-Weston potato products, Golden Valley Microwave Foods and seafood operations performed well.

In ConAgra's refrigerated foods segment, operating profit fell 1.9 percent from a year ago to $379.8 million and sales decreased two percent to $12.74 billion. The fiscal 1997 sales decline was primarily due to beef and poultry restructuring actions taken to improve efficiency and benefit earnings.

The U.S. and Australia beef businesses both reported significant operating profit growth in fiscal 1997's fourth quarter and full year. Branded processed meats, the segment's largest profit contributor, increased full-year earnings, but fourth quarter earnings fell against strong results last year.
In the pork business, operating profit was up in the fourth quarter and down for the year. Cheese business operating profit was down in both periods, the company said.

Disappointing poultry results were the main cause of the refrigerated foods segment's profit decrease for the full year, it said. The chicken products business improved its results in fiscal 1997's fourth quarter, but full-year results were down sharply for both chicken products and turkey products. The main negative factor, soaring feed ingredient costs, has eased considerably, ConAgra said in a news release.

In ConAgra's Food Inputs & Ingredients industry segment, fiscal 1997 operating profit was $352.1 million, even with $352.3 million in fiscal 1996. Sales decreased slightly to $5.93 billion from $5.96 billion in fiscal 1996.

Business dispositions and lower wheat prices drove the sales declines. Placing the large wholly owned malt business in a 50-50 joint venture at the beginning of fiscal 1997 meaningfully reduced its profit contribution as well as consolidated sales, ConAgra said.

Flour milling and specialty foods ingredients, helped by an acquisition, substantially increased operating profit in fiscal 1997's fourth quarter and full year. In United Agri Products, the major crop inputs business, operating profit was down modestly in the fourth quarter and up slightly for the year.

Grain merchandising earnings declined in both periods from strong results in fiscal 1996. Europe processing operations showed earnings gains in fiscal 1997's full year and fourth quarter. Earnings were down in both periods in the specialty grain, feed ingredient merchandising and international fertilizer businesses, the latter case due to a temporary shortfall in Asian demand.
